youtube.baslik: Why can the poorer ear's word score look better than expected? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Word recognition is tested at a high level, so words presented at 90 dB HL can reach the other cochlea at about 50 dB. If that ear hears well, it recognizes the words and the poorer ear looks much better than it is; to prevent this, speech noise is delivered to the other ear.

cumleler: Word recognition is tested at a comfortable, meaning high, level.
At ninety dB HL, about fifty dB can reach the other cochlea.
If that ear hears well, it recognizes the words.
The poorer ear's score then looks much better than it is.
That is why speech noise is delivered to the other ear.
